title: One Scion, Right-Sized for the Device

ciFast.note: Fast verification must pass after the adaptive Scion route is pushed.

ciDeep.note: The release changes runtime admission and orchestration rather than training or benchmark promotion.

deploy.note: Production deployment follows a green merge.

liveProvider.note: Production must complete one Scion adaptive build with zero model download in the observed adapter-less Chrome session.

manualHuman.note: No instructor, expert, accessibility, classroom, or student-outcome claim is made.

manualBrowser.note: Local Chrome passed two fresh adaptive generations, all ten public surfaces in dark mode, the completed workspace in light mode, a cross-lesson source-bound Agent question, slide contrast inspection, and a 35-file physical ZIP; responsive Chromium checks passed at 320px, phone, tablet, and compact-laptop sizes. Production-origin proof remains release-blocking.

claims.summary: The stale GLUE request marker is distinguished from a model-read length, and native evidence identifies the unavailable WebGPU adapter.
Scion obtains a real WebGPU adapter before importing Wllama or starting the 3.35 GB model transfer.

An explicit runtime-capability or storage boundary uses Scion's private evidence/compiler lane with zero model requests and no public Algi choice; source gaps require a clearly labeled current-source action that discloses the course-title/topic network boundary before generation.
A null or impossible native response is rejected before output allocation, real native errors remain visible, and stale GLUE bytes do not delete the model cache.
Large OPFS reads use validated 64 MiB views with consecutive destination and source cursors as defense in depth.
Explicit lesson-count instructions no longer leak into the live course title, while model weights, adapter state, research consent, and quality claims remain unchanged.

A fresh local adaptive Scion build explicitly opts into current public sources from its primary action, completes 4/4 kernels and 9/9 materials in nine seconds with zero blockers or warnings, reports an honest 65/100 automated readiness signal, and its 35-file physical ZIP passes all 38 export checks.

Reader-facing language, reference-fragment admission, dark-mode slide contrast, W3C provenance, cross-lesson local Agent answers, and public Scion export identity remain coherent without exposing the internal prototype codename or a contradictory model-cost claim.

carryForward.item: Record production-origin generation, Agent, console, responsive, and physical ZIP proof after deployment.
Record local-Gemma activation separately on a WebGPU-capable browser when that device is available.
Keep the optional trained adapter inactive until it beats the pinned public base on the frozen held-out ruler.
Seek independent instructor or classroom evidence before raising the Automated Readiness evidence tier.
